title: Probabilistic analysis of dual decomposition on two-stage stochastic integer programs
contribution: First average-case analysis of Branch-and-Price on random two-stage stochastic binary IPs: with probability at least 0.9999 - 1/n the tree has n^{O_m(log s)} nodes, via a bound O_m(s log s log^2 n / n) on the LP integrality gap.
problem_entry: Decomposition methods work well in practice but guarantees are worst-case Theta(2^n) from counting first-stage solutions (pp. 1-2); narrowed to dual decomposition plus branching, i.e. Branch-and-Price (pp. 2-3).
key_idea: Tree size is controlled by the integrality gap through a count of binary first-stage points with high Lagrangian value, using only the projection onto x0 to avoid exponential dependence on m*s (pp. 3, 5-8); the gap is bounded by extending Dyer-Frieze from one block to many under a stronger RHS assumption (p. 13).
assumptions: Entries of c, A i.i.d. U[0,1]; b = beta*2n with beta in (1/4,1/2), the 1/4 bound 'for technical reasons' (p. 3); fixed m, growing n and s; exact dual-decomposition oracle (p. 3); binary and equal dimensions, extension to mixed-integer claimed without proof (p. 2).
proof_devices: Best-bound argument: every internal node has DUAL(N) >= OPT (Lemma 3.1, pp. 6-7)
Charging nodes to binary points of high Lagrangian value, at most n per point, tree <= 2n|Omega|+1 (Lemma 3.2, pp. 7-8)
Lagrangian loss as distances of first-stage columns to the dual hyperplane, bucketed and counted with slab lemmas from [11] (Lemmas 3.4-3.6, pp. 8-10)
Gap decomposition into reduced-cost and slackness terms with LP solved on shrunk RHS b - 2d1 (Lemma 4.1, pp. 12, 15-16)
Dual-size bound by perturbation on typical instances with Chernoff bounds (Claims 4.2-4.3, pp. 16-18)
epsilon-net over duals plus union bound to count zeros of the LP solution (Claims 4.4-4.6, pp. 18-20, 27)
Conditioning on the zero set leaves columns uniform on a reduced-cost region; box-like subregion; Dyer-Frieze discrepancy lemma with probability boosting over independent groups (pp. 20-26, 28)
positioning: Claims first average-case analysis of Branch-and-Price (p. 4); extends Dyer-Frieze [13] to multi-block two-stage IPs and reuses own SODA 2021 B&B argument [11] with the key difference stated (pp. 5, 9, 13); uses Borst-Dadush-Huiberts-Tiwari [5] (p. 13).
writing: Informal main theorem first, then two components (pp. 3-4); 'high-level idea' lists and a 'Main Steps' subsection before proofs (pp. 5, 12-14); practical takeaway on LP-based heuristics (p. 4); proof-convenience choices labelled (pp. 3, 12).
limits_future: Stated: exact oracle, fixed m, beta >= 1/4, Benders not covered (pp. 3, 26). Unstated: no lower bound or tight example, no experiment, constant success probability, unproved extension claim (p. 2).

method_links.note: Explains an unexplained solver regularity (decomposition converges fast) by a proxy theorem on random instances and says what practice it explains
No tight example, lower bound, or failure when beta >= 1/4 is dropped; extension asserted without proof
Gap theorem framed as support for dual bounds of LP-based decomposition with many scenarios (weak)

title: Accelerating Column Generation in Highly Degenerate Integer Programming Problems with Template Pricing
contribution: Template pricing, which picks negative-reduced-cost columns most similar to a template taken from the current master solution, speeds up column generation on degenerate GAP instances by orders of magnitude over Dantzig and Pessoa pricing and yields near-optimal integer solutions.
problem_entry: Column generation with Dantzig pricing converges slowly under dual degeneracy and independent subproblems return incompatible columns (pp. 1, 4); GAP with job/machine ratio as degeneracy proxy (p. 8).
key_idea: Lexicographic pricing: maximize similarity (+1/0/-1 by near-integrality of the template) over good columns, reduced cost only as tie-breaker; exact via hierarchical MIP, heuristic via bisection on one Lagrangian weight that keeps the knapsack DP (pp. 5-7, 20).
assumptions: Independent subproblems, integer costs, root node only, no primal heuristics (pp. 9, 16); 57 Yagiura and 1,735 ISA GAP instances (p. 8).
experiments: C++/HiGHS, shared knapsack DP, per-method initialization and tuned column management; Yagiura 6 h x 5 seeds: LT/MT solve all, RMP time 15.4 s vs 5,285.2 s (D) and 2,642.3 s (P), 10x fewer and 10x faster pivots; ISA 1 h: 96.9% (LT) vs 58.3% (P) vs 76.7% (LR) (pp. 10-15, 22).
positioning: Among dual-stabilization methods, Ghoniem-Sherali compatible pricing and dynamic constraint aggregation; Pessoa smoothing as strong baseline; LR as traditional choice for degenerate GAP (pp. 3-6, 8).
writing: Contribution bullets and five numbered advantages (pp. 1-2, 6); a design-choices section before results (p. 8); fairness language recurs (pp. 8, 10); explanation of pivots hedged as 'possible' (p. 13).
limits_future: Stated: no branch-and-price, simple similarity, Lagrangian heuristic may not suit complex subproblems, shared-subproblem classes need new templates (pp. 9, 15-16). Unstated: abstract's 43%/9% and 'all 1735' claims not backed by a body table read; LT solves 96.9% in 1 h (pp. 1, 15).

Test whether a common initialization is fair before using it; else give each method its own best start (p. 10)

quotes.text: We exclude approaches that either modify the RMP or use alternative algorithms to solve the RMP, so that we can isolate the contribution of pricing.

title: Chvátal-Gomory Rounding of Eigenvector Inequalities for QCQPs
contribution: Defines Eigen-CG cuts by CG-rounding eigenvector inequalities for QCQPs, proves strictly nested subfamilies with equal conic closures (all equal to Boros-Hammer), shows they miss most BQP_6 facets and that dense ones are shallow over SDP+McCormick, and confirms computationally that sparse cuts carry the gains.
problem_entry: Eigen-cuts are dense and numerically troublesome (p. 3); apply Chvatal-Gomory rounding via Burer-Letchford's BQP-to-QPB validity transfer (pp. 2-3).
key_idea: Round coefficients of eigen-cuts to get Eigen-CG; through this lens BH = F0 and intermediate families F1, F2 arise; strict containment but equal closures; depth falls with support over SDP (pp. 3-14).
assumptions: Compact QCQP on [0,1]^n (p. 1); depth results assume the point satisfies SDP and McCormick (pp. 12-14); experiments restricted to BH cuts, BH separator with |w_i| <= 2 and sum |w_i| <= 10 (pp. 14, 16).
proof_devices: Small explicit counterexamples plus infeasible linear systems for strict containment (Lemma 2, pp. 6-7)
Square-free factorization normal form and two-BH nonnegative combination with half-integer shifts for closure equality (Prop. 2, Lemma 4, pp. 7-9)
Sign-pattern, 2x2 product-consistency and 3-cycle interval arguments certifying facets of BQP_6 are not Eigen-CG, automated over 113,088 facets (Props. 3-5, pp. 9-12)
Depth bound: SDP slack bounds the numerator by 1, forced nonzero rounded coefficients bound the norm, 1-D convex minimization gives 2/sqrt(k(k-2)) (Props. 6-7, pp. 12-14)
experiments: 30 Biq Mac binary QPs as QCQPs; MOSEK SDPs, Gurobi separator and 4-h upper bounds; ladder McCormick -> triangles -> SDP -> violated BQP_4/BQP_5 facets from lookup tables closes or shrinks gaps to <0.5% (up to ~20,000 s); denser BH cuts add little over SDP but more without SDP (pp. 14-22).
positioning: Within BQP/cut-polytope literature (Boros-Hammer, Deza-Laurent, Letchford-Sorensen), CG for BQP and for conic/SDP problems (de Meijer-Sotirov); BH-as-special-case known, new CG derivation; complementary to efficient BH separation; own sparse-PCA cuts and depth measure (pp. 3-5, 14).
writing: Contributions with 'perhaps surprisingly' and an explicit unproved conjecture (p. 4); depth theorem framed as complementary to practice (p. 4); closing one-sentence research direction (p. 22).
limits_future: Conjecture 1 open; Eigen-CG misses most BQP_6 facets; separation slow by design; no-SDP runs only be100 (pp. 9, 14, 21-22). Unstated: GAP uses a Gurobi UB, not proven optimum; Prop. 6 vacuous for k <= 2; separator caps limit density (pp. 15-16).

quotes.text: To date, every computational test we have devised suggests that this conjecture is true, but we have not been able to find a proof.

Overall, our results suggest that progress in strengthening SDP relaxations for QCQPs is more likely to come from identifying and exploiting sparse, well-structured inequalities rather than from pursuing increasingly dense eigenvector-based cuts.

title: Extreme strong branching for QCQPs
contribution: Extends strong branching to spatial branch-and-bound by binary-searching branching points per variable with the MIP product score and byproduct bound tightening; in a custom McCormick B&B it beats basic and balance rules on MINLPLib pooling/water instances and solves more FEM model-updating instances than Gurobi (read as arXiv v1).
problem_entry: Can MIP strong branching be extended to continuous variables, where a branching point must also be chosen? Prior extensions fix the point or learn it (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Binary search on each child side using monotonicity of child bounds in alpha, tighten bounds when a child is infeasible or above the incumbent, then score (variable, point) pairs by the product rule (pp. 2-5).
assumptions: Linear objective for presentation (p. 2); McCormick node relaxations (p. 6); all continuous variables are candidates (p. 8); benchmark limited to <= 100 variables (p. 6); binary-search iteration limit not reported.
experiments: Julia B&B on BranchAndBound.jl, HiGHS LPs without warm start, Ipopt, BARON 60 s incumbent passed in; MINLPLib QCQPs: esb mean time 12.30 s vs 57.89/148.52 on 35 solved, gap 8.81% vs ~50% on 9 unsolved; 20 FEM instances vs Gurobi: 8 vs 5 solved, mean gap 7.94% vs 11.26%, 58 vs 8.6M nodes (S123 arXiv pp. 5-8, 11-12).
positioning: Reviews spatial branching rules (Tawarmalani-Sahinidis, Linderoth, Chen-Atamturk-Oren, Fischetti-Monaci, own SOCP rule, Hubner-Gupte-Rebennack) and strong-branching extensions (Belotti et al., Kannan et al.); bound tightening contrasted with FBBT/OBBT (pp. 1-2).
writing: Short note: two numbered benefits, algorithm boxes, one illustrated example (pp. 2-5); assertive results prose ('consistently performs better', p. 7) hedged as 'preliminary' in conclusion (p. 8).
limits_future: Stated: overhead with many variables, reliability-based variant, why it works for bipartite bilinear problems open (p. 8). Unstated: FEM geometric-mean time worse for esb (Tables 3-4, p. 8); BARON warm-start time accounting unstated; a Table 1/Table 5 inconsistency for wastewater04m1 (pp. 7, 11).

quotes.text: This practice is similar to the standard practice of providing the best-known heuristic to isolate the evaluation of the dual bound improvement [10].

Although the commercial solvers have highly engineered and sophisticated internal strategies, these results show that a simple yet effective branching rule can lead to substantial performance gains without the use of any advanced convexification techniques.
